headlines: AMENDMENT 3 PASSES BRINGING MAJOR TAX CUTS TO MIAMI-DADE
COUNTY FACES OVER $300 MILLION REVENUE LOSS
WHAT AMENDMENT 3 MEANS FOR LOCAL MIAMI-DADE SERVICES
draft.article: Miami-Dade County anticipates losing hundreds of millions in tax revenue following the passage of Florida Amendment 3 on Nov. 3 with 61.98 percent voter approval. Taking effect Jan. 1, 2027, the measure elevates the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Local officials project the county will collect roughly $385.8 million less starting in October 2027, with reductions reaching $696.7 million by October 2028. Property taxes currently fund essential county operations, such as 73 fire rescue stations, meals for home-bound seniors, two animal shelters, 50 libraries, over 300 parks, and transit services including Metrorail and Metromover.

headlines: EIGHT INJURED IN MULTI-VEHICLE TURNPIKE CRASH IN WEST MIAMI-DADE

MAJOR TURNPIKE BACKUP AFTER SEVERE WEST MIAMI-DADE WRECK
draft.article: Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to a multi-vehicle crash on Florida's Turnpike in West Miami-Dade late Wednesday morning. The collision occurred around 11:20 a.m. along the northbound lanes near Exit 25 at Southwest Eighth Street. Paramedics classified the scene as a mass casualty incident and transported eight patients to HCA Florida Kendall Hospital. Emergency dispatch traffic indicated that at least two of the injured individuals were in critical condition. The crash resulted in significant roadway closures for West Miami-Dade drivers. According to the Florida Department of Transportation, northbound lanes between Exits 23 and 25 remained completely shut down through 2 p.m.

headlines: MIAMI BEACH MARKS 18TH ANNUAL VETERANS DAY PARADE AND SWIM
VETERANS TAKE THE PLUNGE IN BISCAYNE BAY
HOW MIAMI BEACH CELEBRATED VETERANS FROM BAY TO STREETS
draft.article: Miami Beach celebrated Veterans Day on Wednesday with its 18th annual parade alongside a sunrise swim across Biscayne Bay. Members of the Miami Beach Veterans of Foreign Wars post, established in 1936, kicked off the morning by swimming to Monument Island. Marine Corps veteran Alex Kruger-Dobrota and Navy SEALs took part in the open-water swim alongside five-time Guinness World Record holder Merle Liivand. The gathering honored the city's rich military past, recalling when over 200 local hotels served as barracks for 500,000 soldiers during World War II. Celebrations continued throughout the city with flag giveaways and handwritten letters from local children honoring service members.

headlines: THREE 21-YEAR-OLDS ARRESTED IN WEST PERRINE DRIVE-BY SHOOTING
13 SHOTS FIRED: TRIO JAILED FOR ATTEMPTED MURDER
WEST PERRINE NEIGHBORHOOD SHOCKED AFTER HOME HIT BY GUNFIRE
draft.article:
Three 21-year-olds face four counts each of premeditated attempted murder with a deadly weapon following a drive-by shooting in West Perrine last Wednesday. Authorities say the incident occurred near the 10500 block of Southwest 170th Terrace when Tanyiah Javeana Jones of Opa-locka, James Lorenzo Williams, and Jamarea Letrice Harris arrived at an occupied residence together.

Investigators state Williams stepped out of the vehicle and fired 13 rounds into a front bedroom window while people were inside. No injuries were reported. A marked deputy vehicle tried to stop the car as Williams drove away, sparking a chase that ended when the vehicle crashed on a nearby highway.

Williams remains at the Metrowest Detention Center without bond on multiple charges, while Jones and Harris are held at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE COMMISSIONERS TO VOTE ON SIDEWALK DELIVERY ROBOT LIMITS
SPEED LIMITS COMING FOR MIAMI DELIVERY ROBOTS
ARE DELIVERY ROBOTS TAKING OVER YOUR MIAMI SIDEWALKS
draft.article: Miami-Dade County commissioners will cast a final vote Nov. 17 on new regulations for sidewalk delivery robots. The proposal from Commissioner Micky Steinberg introduces operating permits and caps the devices at 8 mph on most sidewalks. Speed limits would drop to 6 mph in heavy pedestrian zones and reach 10 mph in crosswalks. The automated machines already operate in Wynwood, Brickell, downtown Miami, Coral Gables, and Miami Beach. Under the plan, devices cannot block transit stops or curb ramps and must limit idle time to 30 minutes. Violations carry fines up to $500. A county analysis by Deputy Mayor Roy Coley notes creating enforcement roles will cost $251,773 annually.

headlines: DOLPHINS FALL TO 1-7 AFTER SCORING NINE POINTS AGAINST DETROIT
MIAMI DEFENSE SHINES BUT OFFENSE STALLS
CAN MIAMI BUILD AROUND A DEFENSE DOMINATING TOP OFFENSES?
draft.article:
The Miami Dolphins fell to 1-7 in Week 9 following a 19-9 loss to Detroit, despite an exceptional effort from the hometown defense.

Miami held the top-ranked Detroit offense to 270 total yards and one offensive touchdown. The unit sacked Jared Goff three times, forced an interception, and limited Jahmyr Gibbs to 74 rushing yards. Goff finished with a 17.7 QBR under relentless pressure.

However, the Dolphins offense struggled, finishing 0-for-3 in the red zone and managing only nine points. A 51-yard completion to Kevin Coleman Jr. was wiped out by a holding penalty, leaving a fake punt pass from Bradley Pinion as one of the few sparks.
